name: Missouri
note: In Missouri the funeral director files the death certificate through the state's electronic death registration system within five days of death. The physician or other certifier enters the cause within 72 hours. Coroners (or medical examiners in counties that have them) take violent, suspicious and unattended deaths. Once the record is registered, state law sends it automatically only to election officials: registrars must send a monthly list of deaths to the local election authority and the Secretary of State. No Missouri statute found sends deaths to the Department of Revenue (driver licences) or to MO HealthNet. Certified copies are limited to applicants with a 'direct and tangible interest'. By regulation that includes all family members and genealogists.

citations.title: Death, legal definition
citations.quote: the occurrence of human death shall be determined in accordance with the usual and customary standards of medical practice

citations.title: Death to be reported and investigated by coroner, certain counties
citations.quote: the police, sheriff, law enforcement officer or official, or any person having knowledge of such a death shall immediately notify the coroner

citations.title: Medical examiner to investigate, certain counties
citations.quote: shall immediately notify the office of the medical examiner of the known facts concerning the time, place, manner and circumstances of the death

citations.title: Death certificate, filing within five days
citations.quote: shall be filed with the local registrar, or as otherwise directed by the state registrar, within five days after death

citations.title: Death certificate, mandatory use of the electronic death registration system
citations.quote: shall be required to use and utilize any electronic death registration system required and adopted under subsection 1 of section 193.265

citations.title: Death certificate, funeral director files
citations.quote: The funeral director or person in charge of final disposition of the dead body shall file the certificate of death.

citations.title: Death certificate, medical certification within 72 hours
citations.quote: returned to the funeral director or person in charge of final disposition within seventy-two hours after death

citations.title: Death certificate, referral where decedent not treated within 36 hours
citations.quote: shall be referred to the county medical examiner or coroner or physician or local registrar for investigation

citations.title: Death certificate, medical examiner or coroner certifies non-natural deaths
citations.quote: complete and attest to the accuracy of the medical certification within seventy-two hours after taking charge of the case

citations.title: Death certificate, disposition withheld when cause is delayed
citations.quote: final disposition of the body shall not be made until authorized by the medical examiner, coroner

citations.title: Authorization for Cremation
citations.quote: shall be delivered or mailed to the local registrar of the county where the death occurred before a body is cremated

citations.title: Acts which constitute crimes
citations.quote: refuses to perform any of the duties imposed upon him by this chapter shall be guilty of a class A misdemeanor

citations.title: Local certified copies only after state registration
citations.quote: A certified copy of a death record by the local registrar can only be issued after acceptance and registration with the state registrar.

citations.title: Fees, funding of the electronic death registration system
citations.quote: develop and maintain an electronic birth and death registration system

citations.title: Certified copies, direct and tangible interest
citations.quote: shall issue a certified copy of any vital record in his custody or a part thereof to any applicant having a direct and tangible interest

citations.title: Certified copies, evidentiary value
citations.quote: shall be considered for all purposes the same as the original and shall be prima facie evidence of the facts stated therein

citations.title: Data to the federal vital statistics agency
citations.quote: The federal agency responsible for national vital statistics may be furnished such copies or data from the system of vital statistics

citations.title: Data to public or private agencies for statistical or administrative purposes
citations.quote: Federal, state, local and other public or private agencies may, upon request, be furnished copies or data of any other vital statistics

citations.title: Inspection and copying of records
citations.quote: Copies of death records over fifty years old may be disclosed upon request.

citations.title: Access to Vital Records
citations.quote: All family members, genealogists representing a family member and professionally recognized genealogists are eligible to receive copies of death certificates.

citations.title: Death records to election authority
citations.quote: the state or local registrar of vital statistics shall provide to the election authority a list of the name and address

citations.title: Death records to the Secretary of State
citations.quote: provide a copy of the list of any death reported in the state to the secretary of state

citations.title: Department to keep vital statistics
citations.quote: to have charge of the state system of registration of births and deaths

steps.title: Determine death under customary medical standards
steps.who: Whoever determines death under usual and customary medical standards. Where respiration and circulation are artificially maintained, a licensed physician must determine brain death.
steps.summary: Missouri defines death by statute but does not name who may pronounce it in an ordinary case. Only brain-death determinations are expressly reserved to a licensed physician.

steps.title: Report violent, suspicious or unattended deaths to the coroner or medical examiner
steps.who: Police, sheriff, any law enforcement official, or any person who knows of the death. For a death outside a licensed health care facility, the first licensed medical professional or law enforcement official who learns of it.
steps.trigger: A death by violence, a criminal abortion, a sudden death without a physician in the preceding 36 hours, an unusual or suspicious death, or a death in custody.
steps.summary: In coroner counties (RSMo 58.451) and medical-examiner counties (RSMo 58.720), the coroner or medical examiner takes charge of the body and investigates. Hospice deaths certified as natural by the treating physician need only written notice within 24 hours.

steps.title: Refer natural deaths more than 36 hours after last treatment
steps.who: The certifier, the funeral director, or the local registrar handling the certificate.
steps.trigger: A death from natural causes more than 36 hours after the decedent was last treated by a physician, physician assistant, assistant physician or APRN.

deadline.text: attest within thirty-six hours if the attending practitioner refuses or is unavailable

steps.summary: The case goes to the county medical examiner, coroner, physician or local registrar to investigate and certify the cause. If the cause is natural, the certificate goes back to the attending practitioner. If that practitioner refuses or is unavailable, the investigator attests it.

steps.title: Complete the medical certification
steps.who: The physician, physician assistant, assistant physician or APRN in charge of the care for the condition that caused death. Alternatively an associate, the chief medical officer of the institution, or the autopsy physician (natural deaths only).
steps.summary: The certifier attests the cause of death, by signature or an approved electronic process, and returns it to the funeral director. If the cause cannot be determined within 72 hours, the funeral director must be told why. Disposition then waits for authorisation.

steps.title: Coroner or medical examiner certifies a non-natural death
steps.who: The county medical examiner or coroner.
steps.trigger: Circumstances suggesting the death was not from natural causes.

deadline.text: within seventy-two hours after taking charge of the case

steps.summary: The medical examiner or coroner determines the cause of death and attests the medical certification.

steps.title: Funeral director files the death certificate through the electronic system
steps.who: The funeral director or person in charge of final disposition. Personal data come from the next of kin or the best qualified source.
steps.summary: The funeral director files with the local registrar, or as the state registrar directs. Every data provider must use the electronic death registration system. Knowingly neglecting a duty under chapter 193 is a class A misdemeanor.

steps.title: Completed certificate (or written authorisation) before cremation
steps.who: The funeral director presenting the body to the crematory.
steps.summary: A completed certificate with the cause of death must reach the local registrar before cremation. If the cause is still pending, the certifier must give written authorisation instead. The crematory must get a signed statement that one of these has happened.

steps.title: Registration with the state registrar
steps.who: Local registrar and the state registrar (Department of Health and Senior Services, Bureau of Vital Records).
steps.summary: The Department of Health and Senior Services runs the state system that registers births and deaths. A local registrar may issue a certified death copy only after the state registrar has accepted and registered the record.

steps.title: Certified copies to applicants with a direct and tangible interest
steps.who: The state registrar and authorised local custodians. Eligible applicants: the registrant's immediate family, guardian or official representative (attorney, physician, funeral director). For death records this extends to all family members and genealogists.
steps.summary: Copies are restricted. Anyone else must show a direct and tangible interest, such as protecting personal or property rights. Death records over 50 years old are open.

steps.title: Data to the federal vital statistics agency
steps.who: State registrar to the federal agency responsible for national vital statistics.
steps.summary: Missouri may supply national statistics on a cost-sharing basis. The data may not be used for other purposes unless the state registrar authorises it.

steps.title: Monthly death list to the local election authority
steps.who: The state or local registrar of vital statistics, to the election authority for its jurisdiction.
steps.trigger: Deaths of persons over 18 reported to the registrar.
steps.summary: Registrars must send each election authority the name and address of every person over 18 in its jurisdiction whose death was reported to them, free of charge.

steps.title: Statewide death list to the Secretary of State
steps.who: The registrar, to the Secretary of State. The Secretary of State then notifies the election authority where the deceased lived.
steps.trigger: Any death reported in the state.
steps.summary: This second route catches deaths reported outside the voter's home jurisdiction.

steps.title: Death data to other public agencies on request
steps.who: Federal, state and local agencies (for example benefit or licensing agencies) asking the state registrar.
steps.summary: Agencies may receive copies or data for statistical or administrative purposes, on terms set by regulation. No Missouri statute found requires a routine feed to the Department of Revenue or MO HealthNet.

steps.title: Death data to private agencies on request
steps.who: Private agencies asking the state registrar.
steps.summary: The same provision lets private agencies receive data for statistical or administrative purposes, on terms set by regulation. It is discretionary and no standing verification service was found in statute.

steps.title: Family presents a certified copy to banks and insurers
steps.who: Next of kin or the estate's representative.
steps.trigger: Dealing with the decedent's accounts, policies and contracts.
steps.summary: No Missouri statute was found that requires banks or insurers to check deaths. They rely on a certified copy, which is prima facie evidence of the facts stated.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Certificate filed with the local registrar (via the electronic system) within five days after death; medical certification within 72 hours.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director or person in charge of final disposition files. Next of kin only supply personal data.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of ordinary certificates. Coroners or medical examiners get only referred cases: violent, suspicious or unattended deaths, and deaths more than 36 hours after last treatment.

electronicRegistration.note: All data providers (registrars, coroners, medical examiners, funeral directors, physicians, APRNs, facility officers) must use the electronic death registration system.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register. The Department of Health and Senior Services keeps an event register of births and deaths.

governmentPropagation.note: State law requires automatic death lists only for election officials. No statute found requires the vital records office to notify the Department of Revenue, MO HealthNet or state tax. Federal feeds (SSA electronic death registration) are in the us-federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: Applicants need a direct and tangible interest. By regulation all family members and genealogists qualify for death certificates, and funeral directors may act for the family. Records over 50 years old are open.

privateSectorVerification.note: The state registrar may give private agencies data for statistical or administrative purposes on request, on terms set by regulation. There is no statutory verification service.

gaps: No Missouri statute was found that requires the Bureau of Vital Records to notify the Department of Revenue to cancel a driver licence, or MO HealthNet / the Family Support Division to end benefits. Revisor full-text searches ('vital records' and 'deceased'; 'bureau of vital records'; 'electronic death registration') returned only chapter 193, 115.195, 302.312 (evidence) and family-support sections.
Who may pronounce death in an ordinary case (e.g. registered nurses in nursing homes or hospice) was not found. RSMo 194.005 only reserves brain death to a physician.
Whether Missouri sends deaths to SSA through electronic death registration is not stated in chapter 193. That is left to the us-federal layer.
No burial (as opposed to cremation) permit tied to registration was found in chapter 193 or 19 CSR 10-10. Only 19 CSR 10-10.100 gates cremation on a filed certificate or written authorisation.
No Department of Health and Senior Services agency pages were consulted. All claims rest on RSMo and 19 CSR 10-10.
